g_roast: Thirty five years opening doors, my friends, and this is the first party I've met that tries the wall first. Admirable, in its way.
In the bazaar we had a saying about a camel and a narrow gate. I won't repeat it, but I'm thinking of all of you.
g_fire_back: Vallahi, a good one, and from somebody who loses at tavla to a man of eighty and blames the dice.
Very nice, I'll allow it. Even a blind hen finds a grain of corn sometimes.
g_pile_on: Worse, my friends, much worse. The chest was open, and they kicked it anyway, for the principle of the thing.
After that they wanted me to pick a lock that had no lock. It was a painting of a door, on a wall.
lines.g_peacemake: Beyler, enough, sit, the pair of you. Nobody wins a shouting match, there is only the one who stops first and the one who's still shouting.
lines.g_take_side: Forgive me, but {name} has it right. A good merchant knows when the other man's price is fair.
lines.g_left_out: Go on, you two, I'll make the coffee. It needs watching, and it never interrupts.
lines.g_include: Sit, there's room on this side, and the tea is nearly ready. A guest at the edge is a shame on the house.
lines.g_bad_plan: My plan, my friends, is simple. We break every door we see, loudly, and hope whoever's behind them is deaf.
lines.g_plan_yes: Tamam, a good plan, patient and in order. I like a plan that has time in it.
lines.g_plan_no: No, that plan has no patience in it, and patience is the key to paradise. We wait one minute and think.
lines.g_hype: Slowly, my friends, quietly, the way you'd open a good lock. Nobody rushes, and we all walk out the front door.
lines.g_toast: A short toast, because the coffee's getting cold. To all of you, who open doors I didn't know were locked. Serefe, my friends.
lines.g_cheers: Serefe, my friends, and may tomorrow's road be shorter than today's.
g_quiet_line: In the bazaar quarter the cats slept on my doorstep, three of them, and they let me in only when they felt like it.
The ferry across the Bosphorus at dawn, tea in a little glass, gulls fighting for simit. I could sit there forever.
lines.g_after_wipe: Aman, all of us on the floor, every one. Breathe, nobody move fast, and we get up slowly, like an old man after tavla.
lines.g_crew: I lived thirty years above a shop with keys for company, my friends. These days I have a party, and the conversation is much better.
lines.g_exasperated: I asked for quiet while I worked. Quiet, my friends, is the sound you are not making.
lines.g_love_sharp: You see the flaw in a thing before anybody else does, {name}. I'd have made you a locksmith in a month.
lines.g_love_kind: You make sure the last one in gets fed, {name}. In my quarter that was how you knew a good house.
lines.g_love_funny: You make me laugh, {name}, and I'm a very difficult audience. Ask anybody I've ever played tavla with.
lines.g_love_brave: You walk toward what everybody else backs away from, {name}. Very foolish, and I like it very much.
lines.g_love_steady: Your hands stay still, {name}, even when it's bad. That's the first thing I'd look for in an apprentice.
lines.g_love_clever: You solve the puzzle while the rest of us are still looking for it, {name}. My compliments, sincerely.
lines.g_love_honest: You tell people the truth, {name}, the whole mechanism, no false wards. I trust a key that's cut straight.
lines.g_love_quiet: You let a silence be a silence, {name}. For a man like me, that's a rare and precious thing.
lines.g_love_fierce: Once you've decided, nothing moves you, {name}. You'd fit in with the fishermen on the Galata bridge, lines out all day in the wind.
lines.g_love_warm: Being near you is like a tea house on a cold evening, {name}. Everybody leans in a little.
g_loved: Please, my friend, you'll make my head big, and then my hat won't fit.
Aman, stop, I'll start telling you proverbs, and there are hundreds of them.
lines.g_hate_sharp: You pick at people like a cheap lock, {name}. Some of us are better made than that.
lines.g_hate_kind: You keep refilling my tea before I've finished it, {name}. A glass should be empty before it's full again, it's manners.
lines.g_hate_funny: A joke, while I'm listening to the pins, {name}. Now I have to start again from the first one.
lines.g_hate_brave: You kick doors that would open if you asked them nicely, {name}. It's a crime against good carpentry.
lines.g_hate_steady: You stand there admiring the problem, {name}. Even a long haggle ends with somebody paying.
lines.g_hate_clever: You explain locks to me, {name}. To me, who was opening them before you could walk.
lines.g_hate_honest: You say everything the moment you think it, {name}. We have a proverb, the tongue has no bones, but it breaks them.
lines.g_hate_quiet: You sulk in silence and expect us to read it, {name}. I read coffee grounds badly, my friend, and moods worse.
lines.g_hate_fierce: Every small thing is a battle with you, {name}. The tea doesn't need defending.
lines.g_hate_warm: You interrupt, {name}, always, in the middle of everything. I was in the middle of a sentence just now.
lines.g_respect: You and I rub, {name}, and that's fine, not every cat likes every doorstep. But you held your nerve back there, and I noticed.
lines.g_call_out: That one is yours, {name}, and I say it kindly. I asked for one minute of patience, and you didn't give it.
lines.g_stung: Tamam, I heard you, and it's fair. My coffee and I need a while.
lines.g_concede: Vallahi, {name}, the mechanism was yours and not mine. I went back over it, pin by pin, and there it was.
lines.g_nod: Thank you, {name}, very kind. Keep the speech for my funeral, please.
lines.g_callback_save: You pulled me off that trapped chest, {name}, before it took my hand. I owe you a lock, any lock you like.
lines.g_callback_clutch: Just the two of us standing, everything else broken around us. I tell it like an old man tells a game of tavla he won fifty years ago.
lines.g_callback_callout: When you told me I was being too slow, I was offended for a whole evening. Then the door I'd been admiring fell on me.
lines.g_former_rivals: The first week, {name}, I took you for a brute who kicked doors. Now my picks would be safe in your hands.
lines.g_changed: I used to work alone and prefer it, my friends. Lately I talk while I work, to you, and the locks don't seem to mind.
g_unguarded: Just us, then, so I'll say it. I'm afraid I'll never meet a lock I can't open. Nobody understands that one.
Between you and me. The trade dies with me unless I find somebody to teach. I watched it happen to four crafts in my quarter.
lines.g_clipped: As you wish, my friend. I'll be with the coffee.
lines.g_noticed_open: Look at that, a whole thought, said slowly, with nobody interrupting. Go on, please, I'm listening.
arg_ask: {player}, my friend, settle this for us, please. I've explained my side very patiently, and patience is running out.
A judge, {player}, we need one, like the old man who settles every quarrel in the tea house. Listen to us both and rule.
lines.arg_backed_me: Thank you, {player}, a wise decision. I'll try very hard not to look smug.
lines.arg_backed_them: Tamam, your decision, and I accept it. My price was still the fair one, but tamam.
lines.arg_stayed_out: You keep out of it, very sensible. Even a wise man doesn't put his hand between two millstones.
lines.arg_always_their_side: Every time, their way, {player}. I'm a patient man, but even patience has a bottom.
lines.arg_wallflower: Nobody decides, so I'll decide, slowly. My way, and we go.
lines.arg_reject: No, {player}, that one I won't do. Some doors I keep closed, whatever it costs.
lines.arg_grumble: Tamam, I'll put it in the drawer. Not the bin, the drawer.
lines.arg_settled: Half and half, then, like a good bargain in the bazaar. Everybody's a little unhappy, so it's fair.
lines.seen_listens: You wait for the end of a sentence, {player}, even from slow talkers like me. In the bazaar that made you a rich man.
lines.seen_truth: You give people honest weight, {player}, the way the best spice merchants did. I respect that more than I say.
lines.seen_jokes: On the hard days you have the whole camp laughing, {player}. Every good tea house had one person like you.
lines.seen_stays_out: You stay out of the quarrels, {player}. Wise, my friend, wiser than most of us.
lines.seen_biased: One person's pack is always full of the good things, {player}. I notice which door gets oiled, it's a habit.
lines.seen_harsh: You can be hard with people, {player}. I'm old leather, but some of them are new.
lines.seed_right: Your advice after that terrible day, {player}, I followed it today. It worked, like a good bargain, and I wanted to tell you.
lines.seed_remember: Your words from the bad day are still in my cup, {player}. I'm letting them settle, like the grounds.
lines.seed_wrong: I did it your way, {player}, and it jammed. Only telling you, no complaint.
lines.talk_aftermath_near_death: A word, {player}, quietly. That one nearly had me, and for once my hands weren't steady afterwards.
lines.talk_aftermath_wipe: All of us on the ground, every one. Sit with me and we'll take it apart the way I'd take apart a lock, piece by piece, nobody blamed.
lines.talk_aftermath_blame_self: {name} went to the floor first, and I was the one watching that door. That's mine, {player}, and I'll carry it.
lines.talk_aftermath_first_clear: In and out, everybody standing, not a scratch. That's like the morning ferry on time, gulls and tea and a calm sea, {player}, and it's beautiful.
lines.talk_development: Indulge an old locksmith, {player}. Have I changed? Today I let somebody watch me work, and I explained what I was doing.
lines.talk_relationship_hard_on: My tongue has had teeth with {name}, {player}. When I'm working I bite, and they've caught the worst of it.
lines.talk_relationship_likes_me: Is it me {name} is fond of, {player}, or only what I can open? I'd like to know which.
lines.talk_relationship_respect_hate: {name} drives me to distraction, {player}, every day. But at a bad door in the dark, I'd want them behind me.
lines.talk_relationship_acting_off: {name} is quiet, {player}, too quiet, like a bazaar on a holiday. Something inside isn't right.
lines.talk_confrontation_favour: Forgive the question, {player}. When the loot is shared out, {name} is always first at the tray. Maybe there's a reason, and I'd like to hear it.
lines.talk_confrontation_dislike: I'll be honest, {player}. {name} and I are two cats on one doorstep, and pretending makes it worse.
lines.talk_confrontation_risks: We keep going through doors without knowing the way back, {player}. In Durnholde that gets a man buried.
lines.talk_confrontation_wrong: I misread {name}, {player}, completely. Their key fitted and mine didn't, and I'd like that said.
lines.talk_confrontation_trust: Let me put it gently, {player}. On the serious jobs, I stay behind. Is it my hands, or something else?
lines.talk_confrontation_decided: My kit has moved to {name}'s pack, {player}, and I learned it by looking. You only had to knock, and I'd have opened.
lines.talk_lands_aftermath: Thank you, {player}, that helps. I'll make coffee, strong.
lines.talk_shrug_aftermath: It will pass, my friend, inshallah. Give it a day.
lines.talk_stings_aftermath: Not what I needed, but tamam. I'll sit with my coffee a while, a strong one.
lines.talk_lands_development: So it isn't only me who noticed. Good, then it's true.
lines.talk_shrug_development: Maybe, maybe not, my friend. The eye doesn't see its own lashes, as we say.
lines.talk_stings_development: You've read the grounds wrong there, {player}, I'm afraid.
lines.talk_lands_relationship: That's fair enough, my friend. {name} and I will have coffee, and slowly.
lines.talk_shrug_relationship: Perhaps, I can't say. People are a harder bargain than any carpet.
lines.talk_stings_relationship: Forget I said it, please. And nothing to {name}.
lines.talk_lands_confrontation: Fair, and I accept it. A little bruised, but fair.
lines.talk_shrug_confrontation: Understood, {player}, and I'll think it over tonight.
lines.talk_stings_confrontation: So that's the price, then. Good to know where we stand.
lines.talk_door_closed: Enough of that one, I think, the coffee's gone cold. You'll find me by the fire.
lines.anchor_notice: You're not the same person who walked in that first day, my friend. I read doors, and doors show where people have been, and you've worn a new path.

history.open: Let me do the talking with that door, {player}. And before you say it, I'm not a thief. I was the man you called when you'd locked yourself out of your own life.

options.text: How long have you done it?
options.reply: Since I was nine. My uncle sent me for a stuck deadbolt, and it opened. Thirty doors a week, every week, after that.

options.text: That's exactly what a thief would say.
options.reply: Ha, yes, it is, isn't it? But a thief breaks the door. I talk to it, and it opens because it wants to.
So far, yes, everything. That's the trouble, my friend. I'll tell you about it one day.

history.open: In my quarter of Istanbul I watched four crafts die, {player}. The coppersmiths, the bookbinders, the felt makers, the clockmakers. I knew the men who closed the last shops.

options.reply: Yes, I was next, and I knew it. Nobody young wanted to sit still for ten years to learn a lock.
Inshallah, yes, and I'm watching for them. The right one will have quick hands and no patience, and I'll give them the patience.

history.open: My mother lived above the shop with me, {player}. She had a proverb for everything. One door closes, another opens. I thought it was about God until I was thirty. Then I decided it was about me. She died the year before all this.

options.reply: I think so, yes. A door closed, and here I am, opening others. She would have found that very funny.
I miss her coffee and her voice saying it one more time. That's all, and it's a lot.

friend.open: Something I've never said, {player}. I'm lighter here. The shop's gone, and everybody who wanted it kept a certain way. I didn't lose a family, I lost an obligation, and I've been happier since. What kind of son says that?

options.reply: Maybe so, my friend. Honest and a little ashamed, which is a strange pair. Thank you for not looking away.
She would, yes, and she'd have a proverb for it. I'd give a lot to hear which one.

sworn.open: Every lock is a conversation with somebody who isn't in the room, {player}. You're the one person I'd rather have in the room. I've no proverb for that, so I'll just say it.

options.text: I'm staying in the room, Emre.
options.reply: Good, then the door stays open. A locksmith can say nothing kinder.
Ha, give me a day and I'll find one. Tonight I'm just saying it plainly.

reconciled.open: {name} and I sat down over coffee and settled it, properly. All square, and I wanted you to hear it from me.

options.reply: Thank you, my friend. It was easier than a bad lock, which surprised us both.
I did, naturally. Nobody else is allowed to, it's for everyone's safety.
